proposals.evidence: Turner assigns Punjabi uppar/uppur, Nepali upar, Assamese upari/opare, Bengali upar, Oriya upari/upuri/upara, Hindi ūpar and Gujarati upar to *uppari, the emphatically geminated formation of upari. These whole survey above forms match that retained-p regional series, with ordinary oblique/locative final vowels. The single-p Sanskrit upari article instead gives intervocalic-v or zero outcomes. Other stems, extra words and unresolved expanded endings are excluded.

proposals.evidence: The eleventh *mōṭṭa branch explicitly includes Old Marwari moṭaü big/fat, Gujarati moṭũ and Marathi moṭā, with Jaunsari mōṭō big/fat. These simple western survey moṭ-/mot- adjectives fit that expressive big/fat family, including local vowel and aspiration variation; the relation is qualified family membership rather than a regular sound-law reconstruction. l-expanded adjectives and voiced ḍ forms are not included.
